embeds.title: 🔴 NGINX CVE-2026-42945 Exploited in Wild; openDCIM Flaws Also Under Attack
embeds.description:
A heap buffer overflow vulnerability (CVE-2026-42945, CVSS 9.2) in NGINX Plus and NGINX Open versions 0.6.27 through 1.30.0 is reportedly being actively exploited in the wild, according to VulnCheck. The flaw permits unauthenticated attackers to crash worker processes or execute remote code with crafted HTTP requests, though code execution requires ASLR to be disabled. Separately, VulnCheck reports exploitation of two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-28515 and CVE-2026-28517, both CVSS 9.3) in openDCIM, an open-source data center infrastructure management application. VulnCheck claims the attack activity targeting openDCIM originates from a single Chinese IP and uses a customized AI vulnerability discovery tool.
**Sources:** thehackernews.com • 🔴 1 corroborating
**CVEs:** CVE-2026-42945, CVE-2026-28515, CVE-2026-28517, CVE-2026-28516 • **Access:** Crafted HTTP requests
**Incident date:** unknown • **Confidence:** claim
[Read source](https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/nginx-cve-2026-42945-exploited-in-wild.html)

embeds.title: 🔴 Tycoon2FA Hijacks Microsoft 365 Accounts via Device Code Phishing
embeds.description:
**Actor:** Tycoon2FA
The Tycoon2FA phishing kit now supports device-code phishing attacks and abuses Trustifi click-tracking URLs to hijack Microsoft 365 accounts. According to eSentire research, the attack begins when victims click a Trustifi URL in a phishing email, leading them through a four-layer delivery chain to a fake Microsoft CAPTCHA page where they unknowingly grant OAuth tokens to an attacker-controlled device. The kit includes extensive anti-analysis protections and was observed in late April campaigns after being rebuilt following a March law enforcement disruption.

**Incident date:** 2026-04 • **Confidence:** claim
